- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) or shows strong negative momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true price deviates from recent 7-day average by >2%, model often fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast toward 7-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to dampen sentiment-driven extremes.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model may misalign with trend; align forecast with sentiment’s dominant polarity (e.g., if 70% of sentiment is bullish, forecast should trend up).
